a.text: While you, my unruly shadow—you had every opportunity to avoid involving yourself in this.
But since you decided to jump into the flames together,
Join this magnificent blaze where even shadows lose themselves.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: So we're basically right outside Londinium?

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: That's what I heard.

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: I've never walked so much my entire life.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: You figure you've walked more than Moran and the others?

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: Them? They followed the Leader all the way from the Scáthanna Fields, how can I even compare?

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Well, who's counting? Besides, we're here. What now? We fight?

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: I suppose. We've been through more than our fair share of scuffles on our way here anyway—stray Sarkaz, wasteland bandits, soldiers hired by nobles...

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: Sorry, present company excluded. I meant the ones who specifically target Tarans, you know the type.

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: I know. I just wanted to say...

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: No, it's nothing.

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: Come on, out with it. Is your leg better now? Can you do a little jig?
The slightly sultry breeze of early autumn blows the stench of swamp and grass into the air.
The soldier separated from his squad looks up towards Londinium. His ears are not being deafened by sporadic cannonfire, nor is the Sarkaz witchcraft he heard so much about anywhere to be seen.

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: Fine, I'll try. Just don't step on my leg.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: They're dancing in the camp? I'll tell them to stop. We can't risk the noise this close to the battlefield.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No, it's fine. We'll be safe as long as we're inside the camp.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: But we have to press forward.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The road ahead passes through a battlefield, and I should go alone.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Reed! Moran! Come dance with us!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...So you're all here.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Battlefield's just up ahead. No clue how we're gonna end up...

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: But everyone's in pretty good shape for now, so let's dance while we still can!

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Maybe if we move enough, it'll shake off the fear—

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: That's lovely, but... I'd rather everyone stay here and go no further.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Huh? We're not going to battle?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's too dangerous for you.

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: So you're going on ahead, all by your lonesome?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: How long will you be gone?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I don't know. But I'll definitely return.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Reed, everyone who followed you here knows that fighting is inevitable.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: We all know we're not qualified to join the fray. But we want to help you, even if all we can do is to block a few bolts.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm not qualified either.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Reed?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Be it Wellington, the other Dukes, or the Sarkaz, they are the ones tipping the scales of this war. But us...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No matter which side we choose, we'll make less of a difference on the battlefield than a speck of dust. That goes for both you and me.

spans.text: No matter which side we choose, we'll make less of a difference on the battlefield than a speck of dust. That goes for both you

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Then why...?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: There is something I must do.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But don't mistake me. What I intend is no nobler than facing off with the Victorians for our people, swords drawn. I just... have to face it...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: To face her.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: 'The Leader'?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The Leader.

a.text: Almost every Taran knows of Dublinn and 'The Leader'.
Even those not in the know will soon learn of their existence from the increased Victorian aggression after Wellington's army marched off towards Londinium.
Of course, they will also realize that the Leader of Dublinn standing before them would seem out of place with the fabled 'spectre force', or on Wellington's high-speed battleship.
But she saved them and asked nothing of them, so to them she is without a doubt The Leader.

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: People come and go. Those of us still here have already made up our minds, so don't you worry on our behalf.

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: Don't mind my wounds. I still have a chance against the restless dead.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: You saved my life. Even if I die here, it'll be a worthy death.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Thank you, everyone. But we didn't come all this way to become martyrs.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The road ahead of us doesn't lead to yet more fighting. On the contrary, when I return, we'll... return to a Tara without war. Together.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: So you're coming back for sure, Reed?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Then we'll wait for you.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Thank you.
After the battle at Silverrock Bluffs, the Royal Court forces retreated behind Londinium's walls, while Victoria's Dukes kept their forces stationed around the city, in no hurry to assault it.

Wellington's army, with their fresh new flag, did not participate in the siege, and stationed themselves just outside the warzone like an indifferent observer, coolly watching the deadlock outside the city.
But a stalemate does not necessarily mean peace. Scouting efforts and countermeasures, raids and ambushes, Sarkaz witchcraft and brief cannon barrages...
Accompanying them are the curses and groans of the immobilized wounded, unable to do anything but wait in vain for death to come. Everything comes together in a tapestry of stifling tranquility.
The Draco takes advantage of the current 'peace' and sets off to put an end to it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: How's the situation outside the city?

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: A group of Victorians tried to snatch their wounded off the battlefield a few hours ago, but we bled them dry.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: But... they'll beat us to death if they spot any of us alone, and their firepower's terrifying to boot.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: Captain, is it true? What that so-called Babel on the radio said the other day—

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: Shut up if you want to live!

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: What? A Vouivre walking around outside the city? Even helping to treat the wounded? Is she mocking us? Does she think we're already as good as dead?

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: I'll give you a minute. Consider your lives forfeit if she's still breathing.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: Wait, what? You're telling me she's even saving the Sarkaz?

spans.text: Wait, what? You're telling me she's even saving the

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Bloody devils... They've been holed up in there for days and still pack a punch...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Personally, I'd rather the siege continue.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Old Wellington's not in the siege. Changed flags and retreated to his own camp. It's obvious he no longer wants to fight the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Her Grace the Duke of Caster, in her magnanimity, has ordered us to not pursue the matter any further, but where are we going to find more unlucky blokes to hold off the Sarkaz troops?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I mean, I'm certainly not volunteering for the duty.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Are there even any Victorians left in the city, what with so many wounded soldiers out here on the field?

steps.name: Wounded Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Reporting in. We have... returned.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: What?! How?! Everyone we sent to rescue you never came back!

steps.name: Wounded Victorian Soldier
steps.text: A Vouivre... a Caster, she saved us.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: A Vouivre? Which Duke does she serve? Gododdin? Fife?

steps.name: Wounded Victorian Soldier
steps.text: No idea. She didn't even seem to care which side we were on.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Sod it, just who was she? You're saying she was going, what, towards the city?

steps.name: Wounded Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Seemed like... to the Gastrell.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm sorry, this is all I can do for you.

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: It's okay. I'm just relieved... my chest doesn't hurt anymore, at least.

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: Thank you so much, Leader. I've seen you before, at Oak Grove... You said then, 'The flames have already been kindled.'

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: So now I'll become one of the restless dead, and continue fighting for Tara even after I die, right?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Is that what you want?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Then my answer is this: You won't.

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The flames will indeed swallow up many lives, but never should they intentionally use life as tinder. That isn't how flame is meant to be used.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Do you know the legend of the watchmen? Those who send returning Taran warriors to sleep in flame, so they may finally know rest.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Your fight is over, soldier. I hope you find rest just as they did.

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: Leader, I can't...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: This is an order.

steps.name: Dying Taran
steps.text: ...As you command.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Brigadier, sir.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: What's the situation with our target?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: She's been treating any wounded on her way, but otherwise has been headed straight towards our camp. She'll soon reach the Gastrell's gangway.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: What of the Sarkaz and the other Dukes' movements?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Sarkaz have made a few probing attacks with small squads, but are evidently unaware of the situation and have failed to slow her down.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Continue surveillance, and prepare for her to board. Eliminate any threat to her life.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Another thing, Brigadier, sir. We and you Tarans... have already become companions on the battlefield after risking our lives together, yes?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: No need to beat around the bush. Ask me any question you have.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: I've heard some rumors regarding the target. That you once planned to get rid of her.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: So why are you protecting her now?

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Reporting in. Target is at the gangway!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: (Inquiring look)

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Let her board. Bring her to the command center.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: (Mouthing) The bridge?!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: ...Let her board, and bring her to the Gastrell's command center.

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: I thought... you would have welcomed her personally.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I'm no longer qualified.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Your Grace?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I thought the one waiting for me... would be my sister.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: It is inconvenient for Princess Eblana to meet you at the moment, Miss Loughshinny.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: But I am quite interested in how you managed to obtain the G-0 high ground coordinates. Is it the pharmaceutical company you stay at? That Doctor?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Then, milady, would you kindly pass along a message? The Doctor will have to personally come and get whatever is wanted from Tara.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The Doctor was only helping me meet my sister, expecting nothing from Tara. Only hoping to end the war sooner. And I agree.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Pardon my frankness, Miss Loughshinny, but I see only a mouthpiece here, and I believe mouthpieces have no authority to make suggestions.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I am no go-between. I represent only myself.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Then I shall hear you out.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: What exactly do you want?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Peace.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Peace?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: The cannons still ring, the Sarkaz witchcraft still hovers above our heads, and you speak of peace?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: It is only because I am meeting you in good faith that I will choose not to regard that as an insult to this war.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: That is absolutely not my intention.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: This war continues not because it cannot be ended, Your Grace. Even I can tell the Sarkaz are running out of time.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The Victorians have surrounded the city but have refrained from an assault, in order to preserve their strength.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I suppose they plan to starve out the city.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They do not care if any of their own countrymen remain inside. It does not matter if there actually are, so long as they don't see a single one when they eventually enter the city.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: An ugly tactic, if there ever was one.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: The root of ugliness is cowardice, as it always has been.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: The morality of one's actions does not diminish its cowardice, Miss Loughshinny. Cowardice is when you hesitate to take responsibility.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Which is why I am standing before you now.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I hope that you and your forces can put an end to this ugly siege, break the Sarkaz's fragile front, and spare every Victorian in the city from the calamity created by their own people.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I see. Now I understand why you have come.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: As Her Highness Eblana has said, you show both compassion and nobility. But these virtues of yours are far from a reason for the Tarans to once again involve themselves in a conflict between the Sarkaz and the Victorians.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: The Gastrell would not be stationed here if intervention was never an option.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I asked for a reason, Miss Loughshinny.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I, the Gastrell, and the countless other Taran warriors require a reason good enough for us to risk our own lives.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Please, Your Grace.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: 'Please' has no power on the battlefield.
Reed tries her best to look straight into Wellington's eyes.
She knows well what holds the most power on the battlefield. She knows she is qualified to wield it—and that that right is all she has.
She also knows that once she uses it, there will be no turning back.
But she was never uninvolved, and that is precisely why she came here.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Then, Your Grace, I... I order... you.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: In the name of Tara.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I order you to rescue the Victorian civilians inside the city.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I order your fleet to smash the weak Sarkaz defense line, to bring Londinium the relief she should have had long ago.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I order the Taran army to demonstrate noblesse oblige, not for material benefit, but for all to see our glory.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: As you command.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Any other orders?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You've been stationed outside Londinium this whole time, yet you acquiesced to my command so easily... Could it be because my sister...?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: My presence here means only one thing: that once again, I was able to witness the cowardice and evil of the Victorians.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: As long as you are willing to give orders, you will have command.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: You merely made a choice. To align yourself with Her Highness Eblana, and the newborn Tara.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I did.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I would have come here even if the city was not being besieged.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: If so, then I believe Her Highness will soon find the time to grant you an audience. I'm sorry to say, but this truly is an inconvenient time for her to meet you.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: What is she planning?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Does it matter? Whether it succeeds or fails, it will nonetheless benefit Tara.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...Truly?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: She made a promise. And she will honor it.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Do excuse me.
The command center returns to silence as Reed scrutinizes the conversation they just had.
She completed some of her objectives and learned a few things, but is left even more puzzled.
She has stepped in, and can no longer turn back.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Miss Loughshinny.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You are...?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The general ordered me to escort you out and show you to your cabin.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: You may spend your time aboard the Gastrell as you please before we reach Taran territory.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: My apologies, but there are people waiting for me.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Do you mean the Tarans who have been following you?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The general did consider this. He is willing to send a squad to lead them to our camp here, and let them board a ride on a support ship back to the capital, Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No, I promised them I would return.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Just as I am promising you right now, and have promised His Grace, that I will return to Na Saoirsí.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I believe we made that clear in our earlier exchange.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: My apologies, but I'll need to ask the general about this...

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: He's busy? Ugh... But...

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: What?! With your busy schedule, even...

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Y—Yes! As you command!

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Miss Loughshinny.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm listening.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Direct orders from The Leader. She has instructed us not to interfere with your movements.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: 'The Leader'?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: But she does ardently hope that you can stay just a little while longer.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: To witness a grand performance.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Are you sure about not meeting her personally?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No need to.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Strictly speaking, the war has yet to end. Nothing good will come of meeting Loughshinny now. It would only bring her more confusion.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Very well, Your Highness. Please return to the command center and await the good news.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Hold on.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Seeing that Loughshinny is willing to tie her own fate to Tara's, we should show her the might of the nation she is about to be a part of.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Rest assured. We would demonstrate it with the Sarkaz's prompt defeat.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: But if you prefer a more personal show of force, the Gastrell is more than willing to oblige.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Consider it a grand welcome.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As my dear sister has made her wishes clear, shouldn't I help her realize them with my own hands?

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: Didn't I tell you it doesn't matter where that Vouivre came from? She's helping the Victorians, so she's got to die. Simple as that.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: We're... We're no match for her.

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: You're worthless!

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: ...Bah, forget it. It's just one Vouivre—

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: What was that noise?

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: A—A high-speed battleship! Currently speeding towards the city walls!

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: Victorian?

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: It's the Gastrell—it's that Duke of Wellington guy!

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: Not just him, Caster's fleet seems to be spontaneously coordinating with his ships!

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout Captain
steps.text: Raid! Raid incoming—

steps.name: Sarkaz Scout
steps.text: Purple flames?! Captain—
Atop the Gastrell's bow stands The Leader of Dublinn, purple flames spreading from the tip of her spear to the city walls.
Her flames of death erupt from the Sarkaz on the perimeter, spreading to adjacent victims as they wantonly seek the next host, leaving only the floating Nachzehrer untouched by fire.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Nachzehrer. 'God of War'? 'Lord of War and Death'?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: A shame there is no longer enough death here to sate you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Even living legends have their endings. But surely becoming the kindling of a new legend is better than wasting away in obscurity?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Oh. The brazenly ambitious young Draco.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Very well then.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Red Dragon who toys with life and death on a spear. Just how well do you comprehend death?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I suppose this is not the worst way to kill time before the war is over.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Do try to hold on a little longer, Nachzehrer.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Let us show those Victorians what death truly is, while the artillery still rings.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I have waited a long time, young Draco.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You are bolder than the others.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Then use those flames of yours to send a message to those cowards surrounding the city—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I am here.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The war is here.
The stench of rot thickens as the ice-cold flames of death rage.
Death crashes into death, over the faint shelling and thin city walls.

steps.name: Landless Farmer
steps.text: Th—They really started fighting?

steps.name: Refugee Artisan
steps.text: Did The Leader...

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: Shush! There's no way she'd...

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: No. We have to go find her.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: We promised we'd wait for her here.

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: But the fighting's broken out in Londinium again!

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Just believe in her—

steps.name: Wounded Abandoned Soldier
steps.text: I do, but listen! That's the sound of witchcraft, and the Dukes' cannons! How could The Leader—

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: —Like she believes in us.
The wounded soldier is left speechless, only able to look back on the tranquility now torn apart by flame and chaos. Searching for a reason for his squad to join the battlefield.
Past the smoke and mire he sees a figure.
The Leader. Reed. Loughshinny.
She finished her own fight, held true to her promise, and returns to lead them on, to the end of their journey...
To home, to peace.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Let's go, everyone.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: What is happening there is no longer something we can involve ourselves in.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's time to head home.
